approved: Counter-Terrorism and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2023
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would extend several counter-terrorism powers and add safeguards to police and court procedures.
It would require the minister to consider rights impacts before declaring a prescribed security zone and the AFP Commissioner to notify oversight bodies within 72 hours.
The bill would extend police stop-and-search powers in Division 3A of the Crimes Act and control order and preventative detention order regimes in the Criminal Code until 7 December 2026.
Extends the operation of Division 3A of the Crimes Act for three years to 7 December 2026.
Requires the minister to consider reasonableness, proportionality, duration, and alternative powers before declaring a prescribed security zone.
Requires the AFP Commissioner to notify the Commonwealth Ombudsman, INSLM, and PJCIS within 72 hours of a prescribed security zone declaration.
Requires a police officer exercising stop-and-search powers under section 3UD to inform the person of their right to complain to the Commonwealth Ombudsman or relevant oversight body.
Extends control order and preventative detention order regimes in the Criminal Code for three years to 7 December 2026.
Limits issuing authorities for preventative detention orders to superior court judges only.
Police officers, the AFP Commissioner, the Minister, issuing courts, and persons subject to stop-and-search, control orders, or preventative detention orders.
